study_title: The Capital Conversion Gap: Financing Frictions, Reinvestment Intensity, and Value Creation in Small Public Companies
pilot_scope: 8 hand-selected current companies, engineering checks only
target_scope: Historical point-in-time US-listed small-company panel including delistings
analysis_status: no fitted models, no historical membership panel, no claims of alpha

hypotheses.name: Capital conversion gap
hypotheses.null: Funding source has no incremental association with future per-original-share cash generation conditional on opportunity set.

hypotheses.name: Refinancing cliff
hypotheses.null: Debt repricing exposure has no interaction with credit shocks in predicting real investment or distress.

hypotheses.name: Incremental return on capital
hypotheses.null: Incremental ROIC provides no incremental out-of-sample predictive value over trailing ROIC and growth.

hypotheses.name: Recovery illusion
hypotheses.null: Cash conversion and financing risk do not improve estimates of subsequent recovery forecast errors.

hypotheses.name: Dilution and survival options
hypotheses.null: Dilution interacted with investment opportunity has no additional association with per-share value or survival.

hypotheses.name: Index composition effect
hypotheses.null: Index-reported EPS growth equals fixed-constituent growth after documented aggregation adjustments.

registration_status: Draft protocol in version control; no external preregistration and no fitted analysis
implemented_infrastructure: Hashed raw inputs and offline replication
Conservative capital metrics and partial tagged maturities
